label: input token r
explanation: Token detector: fires on every step whose input token is the letter r, at any position, in both the original phase and the copy phase (when r is fed back as output). It is essentially never active on any other input (only ~18 stray activations on j/s/n out of 199k). Magnitude depends on context. It is highest when r is the last original token right before <DEL> (~0.95-1.0 of max) and when r is the first token at t=0 (~0.95). It is lower for r in the middle of the sequence and for the copy-phase r right after <DEL> (~0.55-0.7). It does not fire on <DEL>, on other letters or digits, or on the step that outputs r unless r is also that step input.

issues: The core claim holds. On the test split, in_tok == tok('r') scores precision 1.0, recall 0.99996, F1 0.99998 and mass recall 0.99999. There are 0 false positives. The only misses are 7 steps with activation about 0.13-0.15, all at t=8 on L=9 inputs j/s/n. That is scattered and negligible (0.0% of activation mass).

One magnitude claim is only partly right. The explanation says the feature is highest when r is the last original token right before <DEL>. The top examples (0.95-1.0) are all L=9 with r at t=8. On shorter sequences, r as the last original token is much lower: 'v r f y [r:0.65] <DEL>', '1 p b [r:0.61] <DEL>', '[r:0.95] y [r:0.57] <DEL>'. So the peak goes with r at the absolute late position t=8, not with being last before <DEL> in general.

There is also a magnitude nuance the explanation misses. r at orig_idx 1 is also fairly high (0.76-0.80, e.g. 'q [r:0.76]', 'd [r:0.80]', 'v [r:0.79]'). Mid-sequence r is about 0.6-0.7, and copy-phase r is about 0.48-0.69. This is consistent with 'magnitude depends on context', but it does not exactly match the stated pattern.
No systematic false-positive or miss class exists. The label 'input token r' does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
